subject: Clarification: routing guarantees, temporary egress, and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Timothy Hansen <tim.hansen@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: DataPrivacy Team <dataprivacy@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: routing guarantees, temporary egress, and subprocessor evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we proceed to procurement we need a short note that clarifies a few things for our legal and privacy teams so we can sign the DPA:

1) Region routing guarantee: can Redwood commit that requests originating from EU customer accounts will be served from EU-only infrastructure by default? If failover happens, please describe the maximum duration of any transient cross-border processing window and whether we can opt out of such failover.

2) Audit logs / telemetry: do any diagnostic logs or aggregated telemetry leave the customer region (EU) for processing/analytics? If so, what minimal identifiers are included and where are they stored?

3) Subprocessors: we need an up-to-date roster (vendor, country, role, SOC2 date) for any subprocessor that may touch content or logs for EU-bound traffic.

4) KMS & keys: is there an option for region-bound customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for model request encryption in the EU deployment?

5) Contract language: our legal team will want a narrow failover clause that allows transient processing outside the EU for cache sync or burst handling only, with a maximum duration and notification requirement. Can you confirm Redwood has an approved fallback playbook and provide it?

Can you send these artifacts by EOD Thu (2026-09-16)? We can then route the DPA redline internally.

Thanks —
Tim
Timothy Hansen
Senior Privacy Counsel | Acme Corp
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Hansen <tim.hansen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: routing guarantees, temporary egress, and subprocessor evidence

Hi Tim —

Appreciate the clear list. I chatted with Legal and Product this morning; answers below and I attached the artifacts you requested. Quick summary first: Redwood offers "region affinity" for EU accounts with a bounded failover window (configurable) for transient syncs; audit logs are retained in-region but some operational metrics are aggregated outside the region in pseudonymized form. Subprocessor roster and current SOC2 snapshot attached.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessor_roster_Q3_2026.csv, regional-egress-playbook.pdf

Detailed responses:

1) Region routing guarantee:
- Default behavior: EU accounts are routed to EU clusters (customer can pin region in account settings).
- Failover: We support a bounded transient failover for availability events; default maximum window is 30 minutes per incident. Customers can request a stricter policy during onboarding (e.g., no failover) — this is a private deployment/dedicated option and we can model into the DPA addendum.

2) Audit logs / telemetry:
- Audit logs (full request/response traces used for security/audit) remain in the customer-region storage by default and are accessible only via customer tenancy.
- Operational telemetry (aggregate metrics for platform health) is aggregated and pseudonymized; the aggregates do not contain full request content or customer identifiers. Aggregated metrics are processed in our primary analytics region (US) for cross-customer product telemetry and are retained per our Metrics Retention policy in the DPA.

3) Subprocessors:
- See attached roster. Key subprocessors that may touch logs or telemetry: Cloud infra provider (EU region), monitoring provider (metrics aggregation — US), audit log archival partner (EU + redundant copy in US for disaster recovery). Each row includes SOC2 snapshot date. If you need vendor SOC reports we can arrange an NDA and provide them in our secure portal.

4) KMS & keys:
- We support customer-managed keys in the Dedicated and Private offerings. For Hosted EU accounts, region-bound KMS is available via an add-on and can be documented in the DPA addendum.

5) Fallback playbook and contract language:
- Attached is our regional-egress-playbook.pdf that describes the step sequence, notification cadence, and allowable operations during failover. We recommend the following redline language as a starting point for the DPA failover clause: 

  "Redwood shall not process Customer Content outside the EU except for transient, narrowly-scoped failover windows necessary to preserve availability. Any such processing shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes per incident unless otherwise agreed in writing, and Redwood shall notify Customer within one (1) hour of initiating such processing. Customer may elect to disable transient failover for their account as a paid configuration option."

Next steps I propose:
- We can upload the DPA to DocuSign (link below) for your redlines — or you can send the redline document back if you prefer.
- Rishi (cc) will pick up the SOC2 evidence exchange and connect with your security team to execute the NDA if needed.
- Grace can scope the Dedicated/Private option if you want a no-failover guarantee.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/rwd/acme/dpa/12345

If that looks good I can ask Legal to accept the redline changes and provide a signed addendum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0178
From: Timothy Hansen <tim.hansen@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: DataPrivacy Team <dataprivacy@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: routing guarantees, temporary egress, and subprocessor evidence

Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. I reviewed the playbook and DPA draft with our legal/privacy team; a few follow-ups before we route to procurement: 

> On Wed, 16 Sep 2026 at 10:14:00 -0700 marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Default behavior: EU accounts are routed to EU clusters (customer can pin region in account settings).
> > Failover: ... default maximum window is 30 minutes per incident.

1) SLA and notification: we asked legal to propose precise SLA language. We need the notification window to be "immediate" (i.e., within 15 minutes of failover initiation) and for the contract to require a post-incident report within 72 hours that includes the root cause and affected egress flows. Can Redwood commit to those timeframes?

2) Data minimization during failover: the playbook says "narrowly scoped" — we require explicit fields: only ephemeral cache keys and K/V shards necessary to resume processing may be transferred, and request payloads cannot be transferred outside the EU unless we provide consent. Please confirm.

3) Subprocessor evidence: the roster looks good but we need the SOC2 coverage dates and latest report for the monitoring/metrics provider and the audit log archival partner. As Marissa noted, we'll sign an NDA but can you start the evidence exchange flow? Rishi, if you can share the access steps that would speed things up.

4) KMS: we will likely request the region-bound KMS add-on. Pricing and timelines would be helpful.

I've attached our DPA redline (ACME_DPA_Redline_20260916.docx) — please review and let us know which items are acceptable vs. need discussion. We aim to confirm by COB Mon (2026-09-20). If Redwood can confirm the notification/report cadence and the strict data minimization statements above, we'll sign the NDA and proceed.

Thanks —
Tim
Timothy Hansen
Senior Privacy Counsel | Acme Corp
